name: vm_cp_root_cx
structural_change: cp1 (the only route, vm_cp_root-cp1-2370c0876): post-CTS TT -609 ps, 9,373 failing endpoints, 13,727 sinks at 356 ps insertion. Path classes read from its 4_cts_final.rpt / preroute_gate.json / textbook_lint.json: (1) pins -> control_code through the accept and next-state logic, 18 levels (rd_i[3] -> control_code[0] -707.7 ps at 770); (2) pin rd_i[0]/wr_i[15] -> the load enable of 2,592 seat flops (io WS -366.8, 3,012 io endpoints below 0; nets of 2,592-5,187 loads); (3) seat/sampled -> SECDED decode -> 2,304-bit compare -> chk_err_q (-531.8) and seat -> decode -> owner compare -> next state -> encode -> control_code (23 levels, 897 ps); (4) state -> fault -> mem_cmd pins unregistered (-341.5); (5) one async reset flop on 5,504 loads. cx1 is a re-timed root (ot_hfd_vm_root_p): every pin is a register (request inputs and rv in the wrapper; seat = slice write-data pin registers; sampled = slice read-data pin registers; four command registers; one tap rank per face; status); accept, seat load (data then parity), command, capture, syndrome, per-word verdict, reduction and load are separate registered stages with per-word replicated enables (36 copies) and 11 replicated synchronous resets; the read row is loaded into the seat as read and the seat scrubs itself in place, so the far-face tap/status ranks take raw seat bits over wire-only paths (<= 456.5 um by a bottleneck word-to-pin-block assignment); smp_enc_q and rd_hold are gone. ~14.5k sinks on one root (<= 15k). Latency measured end to end on the 25-tile bench (latency_vm_cp.sh): +6 cycles per write, +10 per read against the previous root (posted to codex-vm8-service-1013.log). Pins locked per bit (M4 W/E 2 tracks; M3 S/N alternately 2 and 3 tracks), M5 cap, recipe 2. cx2: cx1-0ec026dc7 was refused at the floorplan lint before placement (pin density S/M3 and N/M3 13.9 b/um > 12 over 100 um); the S / N pins are now spread to 11.1 b/um over the whole face (S 12.0-290.4 um), seat words re-assigned to pin blocks by the same bottleneck rule (in-tile wire-only paths <= 482.3 um, die hops <= 497.1 um).
